projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained 18–25 device count combined with zero camera motion strongly indicates a house party where guests are congregating in camera-blind zones (e.g., living room or kitchen). This is typical for Saturday evenings, but worth verifying that cameras weren't accidentally disabled and that HVAC/security settings are optimized for large gatherings.

The sustained 18–20 device count confirms a large gathering, but the complete absence of camera motion for four hours strongly suggests guests are in a camera-blind zone or engaged in a stationary activity like a movie or game night. This aligns with typical Saturday evening social activity, but a quick camera status check would rule out a sensor blind spot and confirm the system is functioning normally.

The consistent presence of 18–20 mobile devices alongside zero camera motion for four hours suggests the household and guests are gathered in a single, camera-blind zone or engaged in a prolonged stationary activity. This may indicate a blind spot in your camera coverage or that motion thresholds are too high for the current setup.

The sustained 18–20 device count combined with zero camera motion over four hours strongly suggests guests are gathered in a camera-blind area or the cameras were temporarily disabled for privacy during this Saturday gathering. A quick check to confirm the cameras are still active and no unintended security blind spots were created is recommended.

The sustained presence of 19–24 devices confirms a large gathering, but the complete absence of camera motion over four hours is highly atypical and suggests guests are either congregating outside camera coverage or that motion detection may be disabled. This warrants a quick check to ensure cameras are functioning and to verify guest locations.

The gradual decline in device count (24 to 19) paired with persistent zero camera motion indicates guests are likely departing through camera-blind exits or lingering in unmonitored zones, which is typical for a Saturday gathering but warrants a quick perimeter check as the crowd thins.

The sustained 22-26 device count paired with zero camera motion strongly suggests guests are congregating in a camera-blind area (garage, basement, or backyard) or the count is driven by stationary IoT devices. While likely a normal Saturday gathering, a quick camera status check is advised to rule out offline sensors.

The sustained 24-28 device count confirms a large gathering, but the complete absence of camera activity indicates either the security cameras are offline/misconfigured or guests are confined to blind zones, leaving the home unmonitored during a busy social event.

The sustained 25-28 device count on a Saturday afternoon strongly indicates a gathering of guests or friends, but the complete lack of camera activity suggests the cameras may be in privacy mode, offline, or the group is stationary, creating a monitoring blind spot during a busy social event.

The sustained high and fluctuating device count (21-27) paired with zero camera activity indicates a likely network tracking anomaly or misconfigured presence detection, as the complete absence of camera motion contradicts the expected activity for that many connected devices.
